content:
elaine: Noticed a confusing API ergonomics issue in the Go generator SDK while helping a user in support. The example in docs shows `StreamGenerate(ctx, prompt)` and then callers range over stream.Chan(), but theres no clear guidance on closing the stream or what happens during auth refresh.

mike: can you summarize the two problems we should fix?

elaine: 1) samples use context.Background() in main which prevents clean shutdown on signals. 2) when the auth token refreshes mid-stream the runtime starts a new handshake but doesn't cancel the old stream's read loop, leading to stray goroutines and duplicated logs.

hiro: thanks. The SDK should at least provide a Close() on the stream so callers can explicitly cancel. Also the stream wrapper should manage an internal ctx so reconnect logic cancels prior attempts.

elaine: proposed minimal fix: change the stream return type to include Close(), update samples to use signal.NotifyContext, and add one-line docs: "Call stream.Close() when you want to stop reading; do not rely on context.Background()."

doc-bot: Suggested PR template entry: "go: generator stream Close() + sample update + doc note"

mike: agree. can we also add a tiny smoketest that runs the sample, sends SIGINT and asserts no goroutine leaks? keeps regressions obvious.

hiro: i'll own the runtime side (cancel-before-reconnect + unit test). mike, can you update onboarding examples? elaine, can you write the doc blurb for the README?

elaine: will do. I'll also add a short migration note for users on Dedicated that may rely on long-lived streams during token rotation.

mike: thanks. let's roll this into the next patch release.

doc-bot: Created PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/4188 (WIP)

elaine: ping when CI is green and i'll add the release-note snippet.
